market_reactions.date_policy: Late-1978 Model II design window is a scenario assumption. November 27 agreement precedes the December 15 scenario integration baseline; no precise historical freeze date is claimed. May 30 announcement and October 15 partner release use plausible selected days, with historical May/June/October windows preserved.

forecast_adjustments.boundary: June 1978–May 1979 sell-through. The June 4 demonstration, October Tandy release, later Apple successor review and confidential July/December IBM actions add no pre-NCC shipments.
forecast_adjustments.interpretation: Replace the prior generic competitor-response allowance with explicit incremental deviations. Apple losses are transfers to competitor sales; Tandy waiting is deferral beyond cutoff, not shipped Model II units; compatibility confidence is a small positive effect. These are assumptions, not measured elasticities.
forecast_adjustments.later_tandy_economics: Customer release October 1979; OEM prices and volume not yet forecast. No unsupported incremental Abacus revenue added to current totals.
forecast_adjustments.bpi_effect: Incremental to already available BPI software: better presentation, demonstrations, training and installation support. Central +1,200 Aurelias; existing positive multipliers give +600/+1,200/+1,800. No double counting of BPI installations as computers; capacity still applies.

sales_reassessment_inputs.status: Alternative-history planning forecast, not observed market data or negotiated price schedule
sales_reassessment_inputs.geography: Worldwide microcomputer unit shipments; Logix includes UK distributor shipments. Five clone brands counted only for their compatible product lines. Other legacy products of those brands remain in other manufacturers.
demand_basis: Author assumption: foresight aligns production and purchased components with finite customer demand. No factory bottleneck or lost sales; no infinite demand, automatic sell-through of arbitrary production, or zero capital costs.

Budget colour and 5 MB configurations enter in May 1980. Native application value, two drives and complete-package pricing improve new-business conversion; IBM has a March 1982 substitute-OS launch, not the historical DOS ecosystem.

Gross factors are explicit low-confidence scenario judgements relative to the frozen same-quarter 1980/81/82 baseline, not measured price elasticities. 1983 uses original 1982 quarters. No historical Apple/IBM dominance is imposed.

Budget purchases substitute for existing Artemis configurations inside the family total; 10/15 percentage points of 1981/82 Logix mix shift from Aurelia+ to Artemis. Clone cannibalisation is deducted once.
Demand scenarios remain finite; capacity follows each scenario. Actual support and supplier qualification are assumed funded, not free. 1983 holds 1982 pricing/costs.

oem_economics.basis: Scenario transfer-price allowances, not signed rates. SGS royalty midpoint of the accepted 3–5% negotiation range; applied only to SGS independent chip sales, never to AION purchases. No whole-computer royalty. Optional board/monitor orders excluded until purchase mix is defined.

capacity.basis: Adam foresees volumes. Incremental capacity is funded one quarter before use, with 5% headroom; no production cap clips sales. Engineering cost allowance, not a released equipment plan.

market.definition: Complete microcomputers, including home/business models; exclude peripherals, terminals, upgrades and software. Shipment-unit share, not revenue or installed-base share.
market.basis: 1981/1982 contemporaneous Dataquest estimates reported by TIME; scope comparability is approximate. 1983 round planning assumption, not a sourced historical count. Quarterly allocation 21/23/25/31 is modelled, not observed. Add only 20% of Logix+clone demand to the calibrated market; the remainder displaces other suppliers.
